analysis.investment_thesis: Indegene is a capable digital services provider to global pharma companies, with a clean balance sheet, positive FCF, and respectable ROE of 20.6% — but FY2025 revenue growth slowed dramatically to ~9.6% (INR 2,590 Cr to INR 2,839 Cr) from a 31% six-year CAGR, making the 26.8x P/E hard to justify at today's growth velocity.
key_strengths: ROE of 20.6% and ROCE of 24.8% with near-zero debt (D/E 0.04) demonstrate capital-efficient operations in a services business
Diversified pharma client base across medical, commercial, and clinical segments provides revenue stability against single-client concentration risk
FCF consistently positive (INR 412 Cr in FY2025), confirming that reported profits translate into real cash
key_risks: Revenue growth decelerated sharply to ~9.6% in FY2025 — a business that commands 26.8x P/E needs to grow much faster to earn that multiple
Operating margins at 12.73% are thin for a technology-enabled services company — limited buffer if wage inflation or pricing pressure materializes
No promoter shareholding data disclosed — for a company of this scale, the absence of promoter skin-in-the-game data is an information gap I dislike
red_flags: Revenue growth deceleration from 31% CAGR to single-digit FY2025 growth is a significant warning signal for a growth-priced stock
Equity was negative at -INR 105 Cr in FY2020, implying prior period balance sheet distress that was subsequently rectified — historical capital structure was aggressive
Large investing outflows in FY2025 (INR 677 Cr) without commensurate revenue acceleration suggests acquisitions that have yet to bear fruit
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Indegene occupies an interesting niche — digitizing the commercial and medical operations of global pharma companies. The business generates clean cash, carries virtually no debt post-FY2025 (borrowings down from INR 490 Cr to INR 122 Cr), and has earned respectable returns on capital. These are attributes I respect. The concern is simple arithmetic: a company growing revenue at 9.6% annually cannot sustain a 26.8x P/E without eventual multiple compression.

The six-year net profit CAGR of 75.4% is misleading — it starts from a near-zero FY2019 base of INR 14 Cr after a loss year in FY2020 (-INR 12 Cr). The underlying business maturation is solid but unspectacular. I would revisit INDGN seriously if it traded closer to 18–20x earnings, which would represent fair value for a ~15% earnings grower with good capital returns. At current prices, the risk/reward is balanced at best.
